title: Chemical-linkage-regulated single-phase crystallization and uniform gallium alloying for efficient solution-processed chalcopyrite solar cells - Nature Energy
gist: Nanjing University of Posts & Telecommunications researchers use an acetate-anion 'chemical linkage' in a thiourea/metal-salt ink to make phase-pure, uniformly Ga-alloyed solution-processed CIGS absorbers, reaching 18.53% champion efficiency (17.53% certified). The result narrows the gap between cheap solution-processed chalcopyrite and the ~23.6% vacuum-deposited record cited in the references.

insights.claim: A solution-processed Cu(In,Ga)Se2 (CIGS) chalcopyrite solar cell made from simple metal salts and thiourea reached a champion power conversion efficiency of 18.53%, with 17.53% independently certified.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Certified ~17.5% puts low-cost ink-based CIGS within striking distance of commercial thin-film efficiencies.
insights.quote: The resulting solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 18.53% (certified 17.53%).

insights.claim: Solution processing offers large cost advantages for making chalcopyrite solar cells, but controlling crystallization and reaching the desired composition have been the key unsolved obstacles.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: The bottleneck for cheap CIGS is chemistry control, not equipment; solving it targets capex-heavy vacuum deposition.
insights.quote: Solution processing has great advantages in lowering the cost for fabricating chalcopyrite solar cells, yet challenges remain in controlling the crystallization process and achieving desirable composition.

insights.claim: The reference list cites a vacuum-processed CIGS cell with silver alloying and steep gallium grading at 23.6% efficiency, implying solution-processed CIGS at 17.5-18.5% still trails the best vacuum devices by roughly 5 percentage points.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: The remaining efficiency gap is the hurdle a solution-processed CIGS manufacturing case must clear.
insights.quote: High-concentration silver alloying and steep back-contact gallium grading enabling copper indium gallium selenide solar cell with 23.6% efficiency.

insights.claim: Adding an acetate anion (OAc-), which can both hydrogen-bond and coordinate, to the precursor solution builds a molecular network linking Cu-thiourea complexes with In and Ga complexes, which controls reactions and prevents unwanted secondary phases during crystallization.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Targeted ligand design rather than processing hardware is what delivers phase purity in multi-element inks.
insights.quote: a molecular network connecting Cu–Tu and In– or Ga– complexes can be established in the precursor solution, which facilitates controlled reactions and prevents the formation of undesired secondary phases during crystallization

insights.claim: Coordination between gallium and acetate allows uniform and complete Ga alloying, producing high-purity single-phase CIGS films; non-uniform Ga incorporation has been a known difficulty for solution routes.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Uniform Ga alloying is what lets solution CIGS tune bandgap, relevant for tandem bottom-cell use.
insights.quote: The coordination between Ga and OAc− also enables uniform and complete Ga alloying for high-purity single-phase Cu(In,Ga)Se2 films.

insights.claim: The authors argue that phase-pure multi-element chalcogenide materials can be achieved generally through rational, precise design of solution chemistry, framing the approach as transferable beyond CIGS.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: If transferable, the same linkage approach could help kesterite and other cheap multi-element absorbers.
insights.quote: Our work shows that phase-pure multi-element chalcogenide materials can be achieved by rational and precise design of solution chemistry.

insights.claim: The method uses simple metal salts and thiourea rather than hazardous hydrazine-based inks, which earlier high-efficiency solution CIGS work relied on according to the cited literature.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Safer, cheaper ink chemistry lowers barriers to scale-up of printed thin-film PV.
insights.quote: using simple metal salts and thiourea (Tu) as precursors
insights.locator: Here we show a precursor linkage
